text: Digitisation was the single largest improvement in the telephone network's history. Why?
choices: It reduced the cost of switches
It permitted regeneration rather than amplification, so noise stopped accumulating over distance
It allowed calls to be encrypted
It halved the bandwidth per call
explanation: An amplified analog signal carries its accumulated noise forward and compounds it; a regenerated digital signal is re-decided at each hop and emerges clean. This is what made transcontinental calls sound like local ones, and it produced the 64 kb/s DS0.
